ground_truth.description: Swapping payout calculator during settlement uses new calculator's logic instead of the one active when tickets were purchased.
ground_truth.root_cause: Swapping payout calculator during settlement uses new calculator's logic instead of the one active when tickets were purchased.
ground_truth.fix_description: Store active payout calculator in drawing state when initializeJackpot() is called.

vulnerabilities.explanation: When duplicate tickets are purchased, the contract adds (ticketPrice - edgePerTicket) to the prize pool to maintain LP edge. However, this logic incorrectly applies the same calculation regardless of whether the ticket was purchased with referrals. This creates an economic imbalance where tickets with referrals effectively contribute more to the prize pool than they should.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. An attacker purchases tickets with referrals (referralFee > 0) 2. They then purchase duplicate tickets with the same numbers 3. For each duplicate, the contract adds (ticketPrice - edgePerTicket) to prize pool instead of accounting for the referral deduction 4. This inflates the prize pool beyond what the actual LP contribution warrants 5. When winnings are distributed, LPs lose money due to inflated prize obligations
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Modify the duplicate ticket handling to account for referral deductions. Either use the actual payment amount after referral fees or track the original payment amount separately for prize pool calculations.

vulnerabilities.type: Logic Error - Referral Fee Double Counting
vulnerabilities.explanation: The contract calculates referral fees as (total_tickets_value * referral_fee / PRECISE_UNIT) but doesn't account for the fact that duplicate ticket purchases still only consume one referral fee allocation. The lpEarnings update doesn't consider referral deductions from duplicate tickets.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. User buys 10 tickets with referrals, paying referral fees on all 10 2. User then buys 5 duplicate tickets of the same numbers 3. LpEarnings increases by the full duplicate ticket value without accounting for referral fee deductions 4. This creates an accounting discrepancy where LP earnings don't match actual economic contributions
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Track referral fees separately for original vs duplicate tickets, ensuring that the prize pool adjustments properly account for the actual economic value contributed after referral fees.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains critical logic errors in prize pool management when handling duplicate ticket purchases. The main vulnerability allows economic manipulation where duplicate purchases with referrals create disproportionate prize pool inflation, potentially causing losses to liquidity providers. Additional medium-severity issues involve referral fee accounting that could lead to imbalances in LP earnings calculations.
